html:
Byblos, today's Jbeil, is a port on the coast of Lebanon that has been lived in for some 7,000 years. From about 3000 BCE it was the main harbour for trade between the Levant and Egypt.

Egypt had no good timber, and Byblos shipped it cedar from the mountains, getting back gold, linen and papyrus. The Greeks named papyrus, and so the book, after the town, which is why the Bible is called what it is. The stone coffin of Ahiram, a king of Byblos around 1000 BCE, bears one of the oldest texts in the Phoenician alphabet.

Byblos was one of the Phoenician cities, later eclipsed by Tyre and Sidon. Crusaders built a castle there. It became a World Heritage Site in 1984. See also Old Kingdom Egypt.
